title: The Undeclared Posit of Potential Infinity

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The literature as stated: Robinson's $Q$ and its models; the rule form of the license; Dedekind's categoricity and the non-arithmetical second-order truth, cited as the classical position's own theorems; the potentialist semantics; truthmakers.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: The corpus: the bounded agent and its record count (5:C1, 5:C2); bounded stability (5:B6); the finite frame's complete decidable theory (5:B5, 00:Z1); the finite direction of determinacy (5:D8); no finite model of $Q$ (25:C1); the reading of a part (25:D1, 00:A4); counting closes by return (00:A5).

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: A formation act of bounded arity yields a new object distinct from its inputs; the paradigms $x\mapsto\{x\}$ and the extension of a finite frame by one element. A configuration is finite and acyclic. In the core a universe is $\mathit{size}$ objects with a formation image, none where the act fails; a trace is $t$ objects with asserted atoms.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: A license is a rule, adopted or declined, asserting nothing. A supply is a proposition: the totality of objects obtainable by iteration exists. Iteration names repeated application under the license; induction names the closure over its results.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The classical construction uses a medium, productivity and an unbounded license. The medium is a presupposition no position declines; productivity and the license are posits; the formalist reading declines productivity coherently. Ontological weight and formal innocence cannot both be claimed.

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: Declining the license is coherent: the finite initial segment with truncated successor, sum and product has a complete, decidable theory and no injective successor missing $0$; on the cycle of $n$ points the successor act is total, returns to its start after $n$ steps, and makes nothing new: every point is already an image.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:posits}\newline \pywit{formation}{p29006}{B4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p29006}{B4} \lean{FRC.Logic.fin\_theory\_complete, FRC.Logic.fin\_theory\_decidable, FRC.Logic.no\_finite\_successor, FRC.Formation.cyc\_lt, FRC.Formation.cyc\_return, FRC.Formation.cyc\_onto}

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: Lemma innocence (i): no finite structure interprets $Q$ --- a model of $Q$ has an injective successor with $0$ outside its range, and on a finite set an injective map is onto. $Q$'s successor axioms alone, with no induction, exclude every finite model.

rows.label: B6
rows.predicate: Lemma innocence (ii): on $[0,n)$ every nonempty subset has a least element, and a property true at $0$ and closed under successor below $n$ holds below $n$: induction is a theorem of every finite frame, for all subsets.

rows.label: B7
rows.predicate: The modal ascent: asserted as true, the license quantifies over stages and possibilities; its truthmaker outruns every finite configuration, since every configuration is realized in a universe extending it by nothing (C2) and in universes of every larger size (C4). Rests on C2, C4.

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: An agent of capacity $K$ over $s\ge2$ letters holds records of at most $K$ symbols, fewer than $s^{K+1}$; certification is a retained record encoding a completed check with a bounded local trace; the locality and interface clauses. Extends 5:C1.

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: Theorem idleness: a check that passes in any universe passes, read by the identity, in the closed finite universe of its own trace, $t(r)$ objects. A record entails nothing that fails there: no count above $t(r)$, no unbounded supply. The sentence ``the universe of formations is infinite'' is certified by no agent at any capacity.

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: The asymmetry: the check of a trace is decided by exhaustive evaluation of its $t^{2}$ atoms and terminates, and the trace is itself a record of $t^{2}$ symbols, retained when $t^{2}\le K$; bounded structural facts are certifiable, the unbounded supply is not (C2).

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: Corollary symmetry, uncertifiability of the bound: a passed check passes after padding by any number $k$ of fresh formations, in a closed realizing universe of exactly $t+k$ objects, so the passing entails no upper bound; with C10, no record fixes the cardinality.

rows.label: C5
rows.predicate: No symmetry of standing: every realization of C2 and C4 is a model of the finite position, which asserts nothing beyond what such models exhibit. Uncertifiability of the bound is a statement about records; the selection between the positions is made at the level of models and costs (\S\ref{subsec:primitive}).

rows.label: C6
rows.predicate: Lemma boundary, Case 1: the disjoint double of a closed universe carries the swap, an automorphism without fixed points, of order two; a condition invariant under the swap has an even number of satisfiers, never exactly one; the check passes in the double.
rows.source: Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary}\newline \pywit{formation}{p29014}{C6}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p29014}{C6} \lean{FRC.Formation.swap\_form, FRC.Formation.swap\_ne, FRC.Formation.swap\_swap, FRC.Formation.passes\_double, FRC.Formation.invariant\_count\_even, FRC.Formation.no\_unique\_invariant}

rows.label: C7
rows.predicate: Lemma boundary, Case 2: the minimal realization holds the trace's objects and nothing else, and a datum the trace never forms has no preimage there: descriptive uniqueness is confined to trace-derived objects, so every presentable object is reachable.

rows.label: C8
rows.predicate: Proposition illusion (i), (ii): the buffer frame of $\sigma$ seeds and $D$ rounds has $\sigma(D+1)$ formations; every object below level $D$ has a fresh image one level up; $k$ acts from a seed reach level $k$ for $k\le D$. Instance $\sigma=2$, $D=17$: $M=36>2\cdot2^{4}$, $D>2^{4}$.

rows.label: C9
rows.predicate: Proposition illusion (iii): every completed check of the agent passes in buffered frames of every size above its trace (C4, C8) and in their doubles (C6), and no act on a presentable object fails (C7): no check separates the agent's frame from any larger one. The classical ``infinite universe'' is the chart reading. Potentiality is the inside view of finitude.

rows.label: C10
rows.predicate: The pigeonhole (O3): an agent with fewer than $s^{K+1}$ records in a frame of $M>s^{K+1}$ formations holds no injective representation of it, so the frame's cardinality is not certifiable from within. Counterparts 25:D1, 00:A4.

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: The truthmaker demand, restricted: a foundational commitment that does ontological work owes an account of its carrier; truthmaker maximalism is not assumed; the deflationist reply is answered by idleness (C2).

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: Under the demand the assertion faces three outcomes: a completed range (actualism, the reductio of 5-reductio, C2 verbatim); a modal realm --- articulated, borrowing the actualist semantics one level up; essence, horn (ii) renamed; primitive, met by declaration, operational content and cost (the fallback stated once); the finite stock, the survivor.

rows.label: D3
rows.predicate: The objections O1--O7 and their replies: declaration (O1); induction untouched (B5, B6, E2; O2); the pigeonhole (C10; O3); not ultrafinitism (O4); the bound undecided by observation, the posit idle (C2, C4, C5; O5); the semantics engaged where the mirroring theorems live (O6); the free parameter (C2; O7).

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: One finite frame; its cardinality determinate and not certifiable by its parts (C10); the license a rule exercised within it; the universal assertion false, its phenomenology derived (C8, C9); induction a theorem (B6); closures as schemas (E2). In the programme the frame is the Carrier, $\Omega=4S+1$, $S\sim10^{122}$ [chart] (00:A2, 00:A7).

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate: Certificate conservativity: a $\Delta_0$ sentence takes its standard value in every frame beyond its bound (5:B6); every instance of a schema below the bound is decided by evaluation; induction transfers instance-wise (B6). Derivations through infinitary principles are kept as derivability facts: a reading.

rows.label: E3
rows.predicate: Effective determinacy: a totality decides every well-posed question about itself, its subsets and relations included, each decision effectively producible; a property of the structure presented as a finite object, not of an agent inside it.

rows.label: E4
rows.predicate: Effective determinacy on a finite frame: subsets and relations are finitely many, and the full second-order theory is decided by exhaustive evaluation over them. The finite direction of 5:D8.

rows.label: E5
rows.predicate: The costs: universal generalizations in schema form (E2); the frame bound unknowable from within (C10); the verdict conditional on declining unanalyzable modal primitives (D2's fallback).

rows.label: X1
rows.predicate: \textbf{``One can always continue''} is derived, not posited: in a buffered finite frame every act on a reachable object succeeds and no enumeration below the horizon is exhausted (C8), while no check witnesses an end (C6, C7). Rests on C2, C6--C8.

rows.label: X2
rows.predicate: \textbf{The finite ontology loses no proof practice:} induction is a theorem of every finite frame (B6) and every executed verification is a bounded instance (E2). Rests on B6, E2.

B4.name: FRC.Logic.fin_theory_complete
B4.doc: 25:C2, Z1, 29:B4 — the theory is complete: every formula or its negation holds, decided by the evaluation, with no appeal to excluded middle.

B4.name: FRC.Logic.fin_theory_decidable
B4.doc: 25:C2, Z1, 29:B4, 29:E2 — decidable by exhaustive evaluation: a formula holds in the finite structure exactly when its evaluation is `true`.

B4.name: FRC.Logic.no_finite_successor
B4.doc: 25:C1, 29:B4, 29:B5 (Proposition noQ) — no successor of `Q` on a finite carrier: no map of `[0, n)` into itself is injective and omits an element, so no finite structure is a model of `Q`.

B4.name: FRC.Formation.cyc_lt
B4.doc: 29:B4 — the act is total: it stays on the cycle.

B4.name: FRC.Formation.cyc_return
B4.doc: 29:B4 — the act returns to its start after `n` steps: the orbit is a cycle, so iteration makes nothing new.

B4.name: FRC.Formation.cyc_onto
B4.doc: 29:B4 — every point of the cycle is already an image: the act produces no new formation (the pigeonhole, `inj_onto`).

B5.name: FRC.Logic.inj_onto
B5.doc: 25:C1, 29:B5 (Proposition noQ, the pigeonhole) — on `[0, n)` an injective map is onto: every `z < n` is a value.

B5.name: FRC.Logic.no_finite_successor
B5.doc: 25:C1, 29:B4, 29:B5 (Proposition noQ) — no successor of `Q` on a finite carrier: no map of `[0, n)` into itself is injective and omits an element, so no finite structure is a model of `Q`.

B6.name: FRC.Logic.leastBelow_some
B6.doc: 5:E1, 29:B6 — a nonempty family has a choice: if some `x < n` has `P x`, `leastBelow P n` is defined.

B6.name: FRC.Logic.leastBelow_spec
B6.doc: 5:E1, 29:B6, 29:E2 (Proposition finite-choice) — the choice is a member, below the bound, and the least one.

B6.name: FRC.Formation.finite_induction
B6.doc: 29:B6, 29:E2, 29:X2 — Lemma innocence (ii): on the finite frame `[0, n)` the induction schema holds for every property, from the least-number principle (`leastBelow`): a property true at `0` and closed under successor below `n` holds below `n`.

C2.name: FRC.Formation.realized
C2.doc: 29:C2 — Theorem idleness (the core form): a check that passes anywhere passes in the finite universe of its own trace, read by the identity: `t(r)` objects suffice.

C2.name: FRC.Formation.minimal_size
C2.doc: 29:C2, 29:C7 — the minimal realization has exactly the trace's `t` objects.

C2.name: FRC.Formation.minimal_closed
C2.doc: 29:C2 — the minimal realization is closed: every image it assigns is one of its objects.

C3.name: FRC.Formation.record_length
C3.doc: 29:C3 — Corollary asymmetry: a trace of `t` objects is a record of `t²` symbols, a bounded structural fact has a certifying record, retained by every agent whose capacity covers it.

C3.name: FRC.Formation.record_square
C3.doc: 29:C3 — the record of the whole trace has `t²` symbols.

C3.name: FRC.Formation.decPasses
C3.doc: 29:C3 — the check of a trace in a universe under a reading is decided by exhaustive evaluation over the `t` objects and the `t²` atoms: a completed check is a terminating computation.

C4.name: FRC.Formation.passes_pad
C4.doc: 29:C4 — Corollary symmetry, the bound: a passed check passes unchanged after padding by any number of formations, so for every `B` there is a realizing universe of more than `B` objects and the passing entails no bound.

C4.name: FRC.Formation.realization_at_size
C4.doc: 29:C4 — the realization at every size: for every `k` the minimal realization padded by `k` fresh formations has exactly `t + k` objects, is closed, and the check passes in it read by the identity. No size is entailed.

C6.name: FRC.Formation.swap_form
C6.doc: 29:C6 — the swap is an automorphism of the double: it commutes with formation.

C6.name: FRC.Formation.swap_ne
C6.doc: 29:C6 — the swap moves every object: no fixed point.

C6.name: FRC.Formation.passes_double
C6.doc: 29:C6 — a passed check passes in the double, read in the first copy.

C6.name: FRC.Formation.invariant_count_even
C6.doc: 29:C6 — Lemma boundary, Case 1: a condition invariant under the swap has an even number of satisfiers in the double, its satisfiers come in pairs.

C6.name: FRC.Formation.no_unique_invariant
C6.doc: 29:C6, 29:X1 — a swap-invariant condition has zero or at least two satisfiers, never exactly one.

C7.name: FRC.Formation.minimal_size
C7.doc: 29:C2, 29:C7 — the minimal realization has exactly the trace's `t` objects.

C7.name: FRC.Formation.no_preimage_in_minimal
C7.doc: 29:C7, 29:X1 — Lemma boundary, Case 2: in the minimal realization a datum the trace never forms has no preimage, so the backward condition "the object whose formation image is `x`" has zero satisfiers.

C8.name: FRC.Formation.buffer_forms
C8.doc: 29:C8 — every object below the top level has a formation image: the act succeeds at every level `k < D`.

C8.name: FRC.Formation.buffer_fresh
C8.doc: 29:C8 — the image is fresh: one level up, inside the frame.

C8.name: FRC.Formation.chain_level
C8.doc: 29:C8 — `k` acts from seed `s` reach level `k`, for `k ≤ D`.

C8.name: FRC.Formation.illusion
C8.doc: 29:C8, 29:X1 — Proposition illusion (i), (ii) in the core: in the buffer frame of `σ` seeds and `D` rounds, every object reached by fewer than `D` acts from a seed has a formation image, and the image is one level further: no act on a reachable object fails and no enumeration below the horizon `D` is exhausted.

C8.name: FRC.Formation.illusion_instance
C8.doc: 29:C8 — the frame's cardinality clause of Proposition illusion at an instance: two seeds, `D = 17 > 2^4`, so `M = 36 > 2 · 2^{3+1}` for an agent of capacity `3` over two letters — decided by the kernel.

C10.name: FRC.Logic.records_lt
C10.doc: 5:C2, 29:C10 (the count) — fewer than `s^(K+1)` records exist for an alphabet of `s ≥ 2` letters.

C10.name: FRC.Logic.no_mirror
C10.doc: 5:C2, 29:C10 (Proposition mirror) — a part with fewer records than the frame has elements holds no injective representation of the frame's domain: no `f : [0, N) → [0, R)` is injective when `R < N`. In the base since task LM23 (from `Theme/Logic.lean`, under its old name), so that the foundation's A4 (Observation; the bounded observer, A5 at task LM23) stands on it.

E2.name: FRC.Logic.stable
E2.doc: 5:B6, 29:E2, 29:X2 (Theorem stability, schema form) — every `Δ₀` formula takes its standard value in every frame `W_N` with `N > t(φ)`: `W_N ⊨ φ* ⟺ ℕ ⊨ φ`, for every environment, by induction on the formula.

E2.name: FRC.Logic.fin_theory_decidable
E2.doc: 25:C2, Z1, 29:B4, 29:E2 — decidable by exhaustive evaluation: a formula holds in the finite structure exactly when its evaluation is `true`.

E2.name: FRC.Formation.finite_induction
E2.doc: 29:B6, 29:E2, 29:X2 — Lemma innocence (ii): on the finite frame `[0, n)` the induction schema holds for every property, from the least-number principle (`leastBelow`): a property true at `0` and closed under successor below `n` holds below `n`.

E2.name: FRC.Logic.leastBelow_spec
E2.doc: 5:E1, 29:B6, 29:E2 (Proposition finite-choice) — the choice is a member, below the bound, and the least one.

E4.name: FRC.Logic.so_theory_decidable
E4.doc: 29:E4 — Corollary determinacy, the finite direction (5:D8): the full second-order theory of a finite structure is decided by exhaustive evaluation, a formula holds exactly when its evaluation is `true`.

E4.name: FRC.Logic.so_theory_complete
E4.doc: 29:E4 — Corollary determinacy, the finite direction: the full second-order theory is complete, every formula or its negation holds, decided by the evaluation.

E4.name: FRC.Logic.so_theory_consistent
E4.doc: 29:E4 — the full second-order theory is consistent: no formula holds together with its negation.

X1.name: FRC.Formation.illusion
X1.doc: 29:C8, 29:X1 — Proposition illusion (i), (ii) in the core: in the buffer frame of `σ` seeds and `D` rounds, every object reached by fewer than `D` acts from a seed has a formation image, and the image is one level further: no act on a reachable object fails and no enumeration below the horizon `D` is exhausted.

X1.name: FRC.Formation.no_unique_invariant
X1.doc: 29:C6, 29:X1 — a swap-invariant condition has zero or at least two satisfiers, never exactly one.

X1.name: FRC.Formation.no_preimage_in_minimal
X1.doc: 29:C7, 29:X1 — Lemma boundary, Case 2: in the minimal realization a datum the trace never forms has no preimage, so the backward condition "the object whose formation image is `x`" has zero satisfiers.

X2.doc: 29:B6, 29:E2, 29:X2 — Lemma innocence (ii): on the finite frame `[0, n)` the induction schema holds for every property, from the least-number principle (`leastBelow`): a property true at `0` and closed under successor below `n` holds below `n`.

X2.doc: 5:B6, 29:E2, 29:X2 (Theorem stability, schema form) — every `Δ₀` formula takes its standard value in every frame `W_N` with `N > t(φ)`: `W_N ⊨ φ* ⟺ ℕ ⊨ φ`, for every environment, by induction on the formula.
